Power supply for banks: what to protect first

A bank has three load levels with different requirements. Processing centres and server rooms require 2N or N+1 architectures with two independent power feeds: Salicru SLC ADAPT2 or Kehua MR33 modular UPS, STS for equipment with a single power supply and batteries for 15–30 minutes. Branches and ATMs are protected by 1–10 kVA rack-mount UPS with external battery modules for 30–60 minutes: this is enough to complete transactions properly and wait for the mains to be restored.

For the head office building, a genset with ATS is installed: the generator takes over lifts, lighting, ventilation and the server room 10–15 seconds after a mains failure, while the UPS bridge this time for IT equipment. The genset in a soundproof enclosure is placed on the roof or in the car park.
Service and monitoring

UPS monitoring via SNMP in the IT department's system, quarterly maintenance, battery testing every six months and genset test runs. AEC Kazakhstan takes sites under a service contract with same-day call-outs in Almaty and scheduled visits to the regions.
What autonomy does a bank branch need?

Usually 30–60 minutes for cash desks, access control and CCTV: during this time the mains is restored or transactions are completed properly. For processing, autonomy is calculated taking genset start-up into account: 10–15 minutes.
Does a branch need a genset?

For a branch in rented premises, a UPS with extended autonomy is usually sufficient. A genset is needed for the head office and the processing centre, where an interruption of more than an hour is unacceptable.
Can ATMs be connected to a shared UPS?
Yes, if the ATMs are in the same building: a 6–10 kVA floor-standing UPS with dedicated lines. For stand-alone ATMs, a compact 1–2 kVA UPS is installed inside the enclosure.
How to monitor UPS across a branch network?
SNMP cards in each UPS and centralised monitoring: status, battery charge, events. We set up integration with Zabbix, PRTG and the bank's monitoring systems.

Guaranteed power for infrastructure and government institutions

Infrastructure and public sector sites share the requirement for mandatory autonomy: emergency lighting and public address systems must run for 1–3 hours, and control rooms and communication nodes cannot stop at all. For IT equipment and communications, double-conversion UPS with batteries for 15–30 minutes are installed; for emergency systems, batteries are sized by discharge tables for the mandatory time; for sites with long outages, gensets with ATS are added.
Supply under public procurement rules

We prepare the technical specification, confirm the characteristics with technical passports and EAEU certificates and attach manufacturers' distributor letters. Equipment from the Almaty warehouse is shipped within 1–3 days; items to order are delivered within the time specified in the contract.
Experience

AEC Kazakhstan customers include Kazaeronavigatsia, the Directorate of State Residences, Almaty Metro and KTZ. Installation, commissioning and service are carried out by our own engineers across Kazakhstan.
Which documents do you provide for a tender?
Technical passports and EAEU certificates, distributor letters from Salicru, Tescom and Kehua, the technical specification, test reports and warranty obligations.
How to calculate emergency lighting autonomy?
Per the standard, 1 or 3 hours depending on the site. We calculate the luminaire power and select batteries by discharge tables with a 20–25 % ageing margin.
Can you service equipment from other suppliers?
Yes: we take UPS and gensets of any brand under service, carry out battery testing and replacement without shutting down the load.
Do you work in the regions?
Yes: supply to all cities of Kazakhstan, scheduled engineer call-outs, service contracts with call-out SLAs.

DC auxiliary power systems and batteries for power facilities

A substation's DC auxiliary power system feeds relay protection, automation, signalling and circuit breaker drives. Its core is a 220 V storage battery of 104–108 cells of 2 V and rectifier chargers operating in float charge mode. Whether the protection operates during a fault depends on the battery condition, so batteries are chosen with a service life of 15–20 years and their capacity is tested regularly.
OPzS or OPzV

OPzS with liquid electrolyte last up to 20 years but require water topping-up and a separate ventilated room. OPzV with gel electrolyte are maintenance-free, can be installed in cabinets next to equipment and last 15–18 years. For KTZ traction substations, we supplied 600 OPzV cells of 420 Ah and 10 charger sets, commissioned according to the outage window schedule.
Testing and replacement

We measure the residual capacity of each cell with a Fluke analyser without disconnecting the battery, forecast the service life and plan the replacement. Rack installation, connection, test discharge and commissioning are carried out by AEC Kazakhstan engineers.
How many cells are needed for a 220 V battery?
Usually 104–108 cells of 2 V, depending on the float voltage and the permissible busbar range. We calculate based on the load type and discharge time.
What battery capacity does a substation need?
Based on load current calculation: the continuous current of protection and automation plus the inrush currents of circuit breaker drives over the standard discharge time, with a 25 % ageing margin.
Can the battery be replaced without shutting down the substation?
Yes: using a temporary battery or running on chargers with cell-by-cell replacement according to the outage window schedule. This is how the replacement was carried out at KTZ traction substations.
Do you supply chargers?
Yes: 220 V DC rectifier chargers with redundancy and insulation monitoring, together with a battery or separately.
